best_for: Developers who live in Vim keys and want a light, fast native editor with LSP support, and who can accept a young project still below version 1.0.

points.title: Native and quick
points.text: Lapce is written in Rust and draws its interface on the GPU through its own Floem toolkit. The project treats any typing lag as a bug, so it suits people tired of slow Electron editors.

points.title: Vim mode without a plugin
points.text: Modal editing in the Vim style is built in and can be switched on or off. You get Vim habits in a graphical editor without hunting for an extension.

points.title: Language smarts through LSP
points.text: Completion, diagnostics and code actions come from the Language Server Protocol, with Tree-sitter for syntax highlighting and a built-in terminal that opens in your project folder.

points.title: Edit code on another machine
points.text: Remote development connects to a remote host while the editor runs locally. You can work against a server that matches production or borrow a bigger machine's power.

points.title: Still a 0.x release
points.text: The current version is 0.4.6, and its notes are mostly small fixes. Plugins use a WASI system that accepts any language compiling to WASI, but the plugin catalog is far smaller than what older editors offer.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Lapce is free under the Apache 2.0 license. The company behind it, Lapdev, also sells Kubernetes development environments, which are a separate product.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 23 versions of the MSI installer. macOS (universal .dmg) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need the GitHub releases page. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub.
